title: Supply Chain & Cloud Application Security
description: Defend against dependency compromise, SBOM compliance, WAF protection, and CI/CD tampering.

questions.question: Which attack exploits compromised third-party dependencies or build systems to breach downstream organizations?
options: Supply Chain Attack
Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
ARP Cache Poisoning
SQL Injection

questions.question: What is the primary role of a Web Application Firewall (WAF)?
options: Filter, monitor, and block malicious HTTP/HTTPS traffic to web apps
Compile TypeScript code into minified JavaScript bundles
Encrypt hard drives on physical database machines
Manage Kubernetes node autoscaling groups

questions.question: What is an SBOM (Software Bill of Materials)?
options: A formal, structured inventory of all components, libraries, and modules used in building a software application
An invoice sent to software vendors for cloud billing hours
A compiler flag enabling binary obfuscation
A database schema for storing OAuth session tokens

questions.question: What is 'SSRF' (Server-Side Request Forgery)?
options: A vulnerability where an attacker induces the server-side application to make HTTP requests to an unintended internal resource
A client-side script injecting rogue ads into user browsers
A DNS amplification technique saturating upstream ISP uplinks
A physical breach of cold storage backup tapes

questions.question: What does SAST (Static Application Security Testing) do?
options: Analyzes source code or compiled binaries without executing the code to find vulnerabilities
Probes running production applications by sending live attack payloads
Simulates physical lock-picking of data center server racks
Tests internet bandwidth latency between branch offices
